title: This app's settings file
description: GET and POST /v1/settings. The file is ~/.config/clawdline-next/config.json, never the Swift app's; its keys are the Swift app's spellings. A write is a merge onto what is on disk, atomic, and leaves every other key as it was. A file that is not a JSON object is refused rather than replaced. Every key here has a row in the native settings window, whose layout is a web page (web/console/src/pages/settings/window) drawn inside a shell window — see docs/shell-bridge.md.

exists.description: False before anything has been written. Every key then has the shell's default.

path.description: Where the file is, whether or not it exists.

hotkey.description: The file's `hotkey`, or null when the file does not carry one as a string. Null means the default, option+space, which the Swift app used to own and no longer does; an empty string means the person asked for none, and registers nothing.

scope_app.description: The file's `scope_app`, or null when absent — which the shell reads as com.googlecode.iterm2. Empty is every app.

language.description: `auto`, or one of the catalog's tags (`zh-Hant`, `en`, …). This build ships only zh-Hant; the key is written so a later one can read it.

mascot.description: Which mascot pack the shell draws.

terminal.description: Where a new session opens: `auto`, `iterm` or `tmux`. Not the same question as scope_app.

reopen_on_return.description: Whether the bar comes back with the terminal.

follow_target.description: Whether the terminal selects the tab the bar points at.

codex_auto_name.description: Whether a new session is named by an assistant. The Swift app's spelling, kept so a line copied between the two files means the same thing.

auto_name_assistant.description: Whose quota that naming turn spends, `claude` or `codex`. Remembered while the switch above is off, so turning it back on does not quietly change providers.

notch.description: Whether a mascot lives in the notch.

y_fraction.description: Where the bar's top sits, as a fraction of screen height.

output_mode.description: What the reading pane shows: `auto`, `transcript` or `terminal`.

output_height.description: The reading pane's height in points.

output_size.description: The reading pane's text size in points.

output_font.description: The reading pane's face. Monospaced, because the pane draws a terminal.

backdrop.description: How much the bar blurs what is behind it.

output_newest_first.description: Whether the reading pane puts the newest first.

voice_settle_seconds.description: How long a pause ends a sentence. 0 is off.

voice_stop_seconds.description: How long a silence ends the whole turn. 0 is off.

remote.description: Whether anything but this Mac may read the session list.

remote_write.description: Whether a paired device may write into a session.

remote_hostname.description: The hostname a named tunnel answers on.

push_on_delivery.description: Notify when a session reports a delivery.

push_on_fanout.description: Notify when a whole batch of dispatched work ends.

smart_notifications.description: Have a model write the sentence a notification carries.

push_on_deploy.description: Notify when a deploy ends, either way.

orchestrator_agent_notify.description: Whether an agent may push a sentence of its own.

orchestrator_enabled.description: Whether one session may hand work to another.

orchestrator_max_children.description: How many child sessions one session may run at once, 1 to 10.

orchestrator_permission.description: How far a child may go on its own: `ask`, `edits` or `full`.

orchestrator_notify_root.description: Whether a finished child types a line back into the session that sent it.

orchestrator_child_linger.description: What becomes of a child's tab after it reports: 0 closes it, 180 waits three minutes, -1 keeps it.

on_state_change.description: The file's `on_state_change`, the argv this app runs when a session changes state. Read only here: it is an argument list, not a command line, and a single text box invites exactly the word-splitting that would break a path with a space in it. Absent is an empty list.

SettingsRequest.description: The keys to change. A null key is left as it is.

hotkey.description: A combination the shell can register (`cmd+shift+k`), or empty for none.

scope_app.description: Bundle identifiers separated by commas, or empty for every app.

language.description: `auto` or a language tag the catalog resolves.

mascot.description: A pack name the shell offers.

reopen_on_return.description: Whether the bar comes back with the terminal.

follow_target.description: Whether the terminal selects the tab the bar points at.
